plate_decision.firelit_layered_REJECTED_reason: The --layered premise ('firelit rides the locked geometry, preserving registration') is EMPIRICALLY FALSE. Edge-recall vs greybox structural edges: pass1 ControlNet base = 1.000, pass2 Gemini detail/populate = 0.873, pass3 Gemini staging (final) = 0.708. The Gemini instruction-edit passes have NO strength knob and RECOMPOSED the geometry — the staging pass invented a central staircase and shifted the left-half floor/walls off the greybox (see overlay_conditioned_crypt.jpg). A 0.708-registered plate would re-misalign the WOSRelight depth/normal sidecars — the ORIGINAL #1469 failure mode. So 'firelit AND 1:1-registered' is UNATTAINABLE via this pipeline; the fair A/B was run on the registered (cool) base instead.

verdict: The #1479 LOSS IS RESOLVED but there is NO decisive WIN. B (relit) and A (flat) are numerically TIED at median 2.0 — yet all 5 scorers RANKED B > A (the forced-ranking tiebreak favored the relit arm every time). Verified in-frame: the shader ambient floor (_AmbLift=0.80) eliminated the black-block voids — pillars, sarcophagus and walls now render as readable painted stone, not solid black (the sole binding defect from #1479 is gone; B went from 2.0<3.0 LOSING to 2.0=2.0 TIED/marginally-preferred). B does NOT beat A decisively because the ONLY plate that registers 1:1 (the single-pass ControlNet base) is cool/flat/low-key — RungB Analyze() sampled a COOL key (DDE0FF), so the relight adds only mild cool directional shaping, not warm firelit cohesion. Both arms score far below the control (2.0 vs 8.0): a ~6-point gap driven by the dull cool plate + dark empty crypt room (a plate-quality confound that drags BOTH arms, not a relight defect).
recommendation: STOP the relight-shader A/B iteration loop; the shader is now CORRECT and NO-HARM (merge it — additive, byte-compatible, resolves the void failure, marginally preferred 5/5). Do NOT port relight to the shipped path yet. The remaining ~6-point gap is NOT a relight-shader problem — it is a PLATE-PIPELINE problem, and the two prescribed fixes are now MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: you can have 1:1 REGISTRATION (single-pass ControlNet, but COOL) OR a WARM firelit plate (--layered, but registration drops to 0.708), never both. Progress on the relight is therefore BLOCKED on a new work item: a plate pipeline that yields a WARM firelit plate at ~1.0 registration (e.g. a ControlNet base that keeps the warm painterly grade, or feeding warmth via the LIGHT RIG on a neutral registered plate rather than sampling it from a cool plate). This is out of scope of 'relight iteration' — hence STOP here.
